KEY MESSAGE 1...

In the mid/upper-levels, a shortwave trough was currently ejecting 
over the Ohio River Valley, with an inverted trough farther upstream 
that was digging southward into the Corn Belt. The former feature is 
responsible for the ongoing rain shield moving eastward across the 
CWA in congruence with the surface and mid-level cold front, and a 
couple of lightning strikes have been observed so far this early 
morning. Recent WSR-88D imagery continues to indicate a downward 
trend in convective organization, and the potential for lightning is 
rapidly diminishing, with a transition to stratiform rain expected 
for the remainder of the predawn hours. This leading band of rain 
will exit the CWA prior to sunrise, with chances for rain showers 
reloading later this morning as the two shortwave troughs phase over 
the region and causes additional moistening of the theta surfaces 
aloft. The CWA will be under the influence of large-scale troughing 
through the first half of the weekend before it attenuates in 
amplitude and shifts off the Eastern Seaboard.

At the surface, the primary cold front responsible for the ongoing 
rain was located along a line from PKB-CRW-LNP, and connects to a 
cyclone in southeastern OH. Farther west, the secondary cold front 
of polar origin trails not far behind, and branches southwestward 
from a deepening surface low near CVG. This polar cold front is 
expected to cross into the CWA shortly after sunrise, with brisk, 
northwesterly winds in its wake. METAR observations across the Rust 
Belt have consistently indicated wind gusts topping out near 20 mph
immediately behind the cold front. Thick, low-level overcast will 
continue to advect into the CWA following the passage of both of 
these fronts; and high temperatures for today were shaved a few 
degrees to account for the strong CAA and restrictions to diabatic 
heating from the overcast. Northwesterly wind gusts between 20-25 
mph are forecast through most of the day, with the gust factor 
diminishing after sunset in the lowlands while the stronger gusts 
persist across the higher terrain into tonight. Off-and-on rain 
showers are expected area-wide today, with the convection (no 
lightning) remaining low-topped.

A transition to a rain-snow mix will occur across the mountains 
tonight, with an expectation for all snow prior to sunrise Friday 
across those locales. However, precipitation intensity is forecast 
to weaken as the base of the large-scale trough shifts south of the 
CWA. Therefore, only a light coating is forecast for the higher 
terrain tonight into Friday morning. A brief lull in precipitation 
should follow into the afternoon hours Friday ahead of another 
shortwave perturbation embedded ejects over the region. Upon the 
arrival of this feature, renewed moistening of the mid-level theta 
surfaces will occur, which will foster the return of snow showers 
across the mountains. Forecast soundings indicate thermal profiles 
that are unfavorable for the growth of large dendrites; however, the 
sub-freezing columns will be saturated with respect to water and, 
therefore, supersaturated with respect to ice. Lower vapor densities 
in the supersaturated columns lean toward the formation of smaller, 
plate-like crystals, so even if locally heavier bursts of snow 
occur, rapid accumulations are not forecast with this event.

Total snow accumulations have trended slightly downward from the 
previous forecasts, with 2-3" of snow forecast across the mountains 
beginning Friday night and lasting into Saturday. Locally higher 
amounts of snow will be possible. Some snow may occur along and east 
of the I-79 corridor Saturday morning as wet-bulb temperatures fall 
below freezing, but accumulations of snow are not expected in the 
lowlands. Lingering snow showers are forecast across the mountains 
Saturday afternoon and into early Sunday morning before finally 
diminishing, although flurries will be possible heading into Sunday 
night. Drier and gradually warmer weather is forecast to return by 
next week as a shortwave ridge shifts eastward towards the region.
